newsitem.title: UK: Firmer business prevails on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Firmer business prevails on sugar freight market.

text.p: Fixtures continued to emerge on London's sugar freight market on Thursday but new inquiry appeared to be slackening towards the end of the week, shipbrokers said.
E D & F Man quoted for 19/20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Casablanca plus Black Sea options for mid-April.

Cargill was said to have fixed its bulk order for 11/12,000 tonnes from Rio Haina to US Gulf/Atlantic for early April and also a further 14,000 tonnes from Buenaventura to the same destinations for March/April.
Rates reported for the latter fixture were $18 for the Gulf, $19 for Savannah and $20 for Baltimore/New York, shipbrokers said.
The 26,715 dwt "Cherry Flower", fixed on timecharter from Queensland to Korea for an early April trip, was said to be booked to carry sugar at a daily rate of $5,800 with $80,000 bonus to Pan Ocean.

Shipbrokers reported a rate of $31.50 achieved on a recent order for 25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio to Black Sea for end-March, some $3 higher than the last rate for a similar inquiry. The charterer was unnamed.
In other news, Syria tendered to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws to be shipped between April 15 and May 15.
March 26 was set as the final date to receive offers.
